questions.question: Why does the Task Tracker use `task.id` as the list `key` instead of the array index?
options: Indexes are slower to compute than UUIDs
A stable, unique key lets React correctly track each item's identity across re-renders, even when the list is reordered or filtered
React requires keys to be strings, and indexes are numbers
There is no real difference between the two approaches
questions.explanation: If the list is filtered, sorted, or reordered, an index-based key can point to the wrong item after a re-render, causing state/UI to attach to the wrong row.

questions.question: Why does `toggleTask` use `prev.map(...)` to build a new array instead of mutating `tasks` directly?
options: map() is the only array method available in React
React detects changes by comparing references; returning a new array is what signals that state actually changed
Mutating arrays throws a runtime error in React
It has no effect on correctness, only style
questions.explanation: React's re-render triggering relies on new state references; mutating the existing array in place wouldn't reliably trigger a re-render.

questions.question: In the Task Tracker, where do `addTask`, `toggleTask`, and `deleteTask` live, and why?
options: Inside each child component separately, for encapsulation
In the top-level TaskTracker component, so all mutations happen in one place and children just receive data and callbacks
In a global variable outside React
questions.explanation: Centralizing mutations in the parent (lifting state up) keeps data flow predictable — TaskForm and TaskList are purely presentational, driven by props.

questions.question: What role does the custom `useLocalStorage` hook play in this project?
options: It replaces useState entirely with a faster alternative
It wraps useState + useEffect so state is automatically persisted to and restored from localStorage
It fetches tasks from a remote API
It is only used for styling
questions.explanation: useLocalStorage reads an initial value from localStorage on mount and writes the value back to localStorage whenever it changes, giving persistence with one line of code in the component.
